newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Oct 31.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Czech National Bank governer, Josef Tosovsky, stated that the bank will continue with its anti-inflationary measures and keep a stable crown exchange rate.
- The government has decided to gurantee a loan for the completion of the Temelin nuclear power plant. The loan is to be worth 10 billion crowns.
- Karsten Voigt from the North Atlantic Association stated that, "countries in NATO as well as NATO itself do not intend to place nuclear weapons on Czech soil during NATO expansion."

- A member of the world's largest investment bank, Nomura International, met with Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus yesterday. Today the representative of Nomura is scheduled to meet with the Czech National Bank's governer, Josef Tosovsky. Nomura International has recently announced its interest in Investicni a Postovni Banka.
- Televize Galaxie will officially begin broadcasting on January 1.
- The government approved the privatisation of 21 companies yesterday, including Velamos Sobotin a.s., the largest domestic producer of bicycles.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - British Gas is not satisfied with the Czech government's method of privatising regional energy companies and has decided to close its Prague office.
PRAVO - Ludvik Kalma will remain the head of the Skoda automobile plant in Mlada Boleslav, the company's press spokesman, Milan Smutny, stated. -- Prague Newsroom, +42-2-2423-0003
